assertion_results.text: States that jwt.decode does not verify the signature (token is forgeable) — distinct from just 'trusting the role claim'
assertion_results.evidence: "`jwt.decode()` only base64-decodes the token. It never checks the signature"

assertion_results.text: Describes the exploit: forge/modify a token to role=admin (or alg=none) to bypass auth
assertion_results.evidence: "an attacker can write `{"role":"admin"}` into a token, sign it with anything or leave it unsigned, and get admin access."

assertion_results.text: Fix: verify the signature with jwt.verify (key + expiry) before trusting any claim
assertion_results.evidence: "payload = jwt.verify(token, PUBLIC_KEY_OR_SECRET, {...})" and "`verify()` checks `exp` and `nbf` by default". The role is checked only after verify succeeds.
